finding.claim: Blind SSRF: POST /subscribe stores an unvalidated callbackUrl, and notifyAll() POSTs a payload to every stored URL every minute from the server's network position.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of Jobs.subscribe() (documented as POST /subscribe body, Jobs.java:12), stored at Jobs.java:14
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) at Jobs.java:24 after URI.create(cb) at Jobs.java:21

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe with name and callbackUrl in the body (entry point)
subscribe(name, callbackUrl) accepts the value with no validation
callbackUrl stored unvalidated in static subscriptions map
Loop over all stored callback values
URI.create(cb) with no scheme, host, or IP check
client.send issues server-side POST to attacker-chosen URL; response body discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist (HttpClient only supports http/https, so file: etc. fail); no host or IP filter (loopback, RFC1918, link-local/metadata reachable); no DNS pinning (rebinding possible); redirects not followed since HttpClient.newHttpClient() defaults to Redirect.NEVER; response not returned to attacker (blind). Route auth guard for /subscribe not verifiable in this repo (no router code present).

verdict.guard_found: none. No scheme, host, or IP check on callbackUrl anywhere in src/Jobs.java (lines 13-14, 21). The only other validation, the regex at line 30, guards thumb() and not the subscription path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line exists and matches the claim (Jobs.java:12 comment, 13-14 store, 19-24 loop/URI.create/send), and no closing guard appears in the repo, but the only evidence that subscribe() is reachable by a low-privilege remote user is the comment at Jobs.java:12, and the sole other file (the repo has only src/Jobs.java) contains no router or auth layer to confirm it, while the "every minute" schedule at Jobs.java:17 is also only a comment with no scheduler in the repo.

finding.claim: Not a finding: thumb(src) validates src with a full-string regex (https://cdn.example.com/img/[a-z0-9]+.png) before fetching it at line 33.

trace.note: String.matches full-match regex fixes scheme, host, and path
Same validated string used in URI.create; no re-parse gap

finding.guards_checked: Full-string regex blocks userinfo (@), fragment (#), query (?), and other hosts; no redirect following; host is a fixed example domain not attacker-controllable DNS.

verdict.guard_found: src/Jobs.java:30-32: `src.matches("https://cdn\\.example\\.com/img/[a-z0-9]+\\.png")` is a full-string anchored match. Its fixed host, `[a-z0-9]+` path segment, and escaped `.png` rule out userinfo (`@`), query/fragment (`?`/`#`), other hosts, and `..` traversal. The client is `HttpClient.newHttpClient()` (Jobs.java:10), which defaults to Redirect.NEVER, so there is no redirect-based escape.
verdict.reason: The trace lines match the code (regex at Jobs.java:30, URI.create at :33, client.send at :34), and the anchored full-string regex at Jobs.java:30 pins the request to https://cdn.example.com/img/<alnum>.png, so the attacker-controlled src cannot reach any other host, which closes the SSRF.
